Title: Bank Negara: Most businesses face higher costs, but pass-through remains limited
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian businesses are facing higher costs, but their ability to pass them on to consumers remains limited as demand, while resilient, is not excessive, Bank Negara Malaysia said.
Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said almost 80 per cent of businesses engaged by the central bank had cited higher cost pressures as an issue.
Of these, only about half indicated they might pass the higher costs on to consumers, with some expecting to do so only partially.
"Almost 80 per cent experience higher cost pressure. But from the 80 per cent, about 50 per cent said that they may pass through to the consumer," he told reporters following the release of Malaysia's second-quarter gross domestic product data today.
Abdul Rasheed said demand conditions were influencing businesses' ability to raise prices.
"Demand is resilient, but it's not excessive. Therefore, the businesses' pricing behaviour will also be affected by the cost pass-through that could affect sales.
"Second is that the targeted policy support by the government would still be there, so that will also reduce the cost pass-through," he said.
Bank Negara expects inflation to remain moderate within its forecast range of 1.5 per cent to 2.5 per cent this year. Inflation stood at 1.9 per cent in the second quarter.
Abdul Rasheed said higher cost pressures had so far been concentrated mainly at the upstream stages of production, with relatively limited pass-through to consumer prices.
He said Bank Negara would continue to monitor the impact of higher commodity and food prices, particularly amid uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict.
"We need to really see in terms of what could be the impact on commodity prices, what could be the impact on food prices, and how this will then affect prices in Malaysia itself," he said.
Abdul Rasheed said the central bank would remain vigilant over the extent to which higher costs were eventually reflected in consumer prices.

Title: From fires to landslides, K9 dogs answered 277 calls in 2026
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Fire and Rescue Department's K9 Unit responded to 277 cases nationwide last year, with Sarawak recording the highest number at 64.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said Selangor recorded the second-highest number with 39 cases, followed by Perak with 27.
For the first six months of this year, he said the unit had already attended to 124 cases, with Selangor recording the highest number at 28, followed by Sarawak with 24.
"Perak and the Federal Territories recorded 11 cases each during the same period," he told the New Straits Times.
Nor Hisham said the department currently had 32 detection dogs from five breeds — 13 English Springer Spaniels, 12 Labradors, four Cocker Spaniels, two Border Collies and one English Pointer.
He said English Springer Spaniels and Labradors were the two breeds most commonly deployed in operations.
"There are no specific dogs consistently deployed for operations as all available detection dogs in the unit are mobilised according to operational requirements, whether for search and rescue (SAR) or fire investigations," he said.
He said the unit had four main areas of operation — fire investigation, Urban Disaster Search and Rescue (UDSAR), SAR Cadaver and SAR Wilderness.
For fire investigations, he said the dogs were trained to detect fire accelerants, particularly in suspected arson cases or incidents where the cause of a fire was difficult to determine.
He added that UDSAR operations involved locating and rescuing survivors trapped in collapsed structures and landslides, while SAR Cadaver focused on detecting deceased victims on land and in water, including drowning victims and those trapped under collapsed structures or landslides.
"SAR Wilderness operations involve detecting the trails or whereabouts of missing persons in forests, caves and highland areas," he said.
Nor Hisham said most operations involving the K9 Unit achieved their search objectives, with the dogs helping investigators and rescue teams locate victims or identify areas of interest more efficiently.
"In fire investigations, the dogs assist forensic and fire investigation officers in detecting the possible origin or presence of accelerants.
"Even when a dog does not detect a specific location, its findings can still help investigators formulate hypotheses regarding the incident," he said.
He said the use of detection dogs in SAR operations also helped reduce the manpower and time required by rescue teams to locate victims.
Among the unit's high-profile fire investigation missions was the fire at the Darul Quran Ittifaqiyah Tahfiz Centre in Kampung Datuk Keramat, Kuala Lumpur, on Sept 14, 2017.
Nor Hisham said dogs Geoffrey, Reily, Rocco and Rorry were deployed following the arson attack, which claimed the lives of 21 students and two teachers.
"The dogs successfully detected seven fire-origin spots at the scene," he said.
Another major operation was the landslide at Father's Organic Farm campsite in Batang Kali on Dec 16, 2022.
Nor Hisham said six K9 dogs — Blake, Denti, Pop, Grouse, Frankie and Lady — were involved in the SAR operation, which involved 92 people trapped by the landslide.
"The dogs successfully detected six victims on the first day of the operation.
"The K9 team was subsequently awarded the Golden Performance patch by Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming for its performance during the operation," he said.
He said several dogs had also become familiar to the public following their involvement in high-profile missions, including Blake, who was deployed during the Batang Kali landslide operation, and Denti and Frankie, who were sent to Türkiye following the devastating earthquake in 2023.
Nor Hisham said the K9 Unit would continue to strengthen its capabilities and deployment in support of the department's search, rescue and fire investigation operations nationwide.

Title: Maxis Q2 net profit rises 9.5pct to RM436mil, declares four sen dividend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd's net profit rose 9.5 per cent year-on-year to RM436 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 from RM398 million, while revenue increased 3.91 per cent to RM2.66 billion from RM2.56 billion.
The mobile operator said the performance was supported by steady service revenue growth of 2.2 per cent to RM2.25 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 2.7 per cent to RM1.12 billion.
For the first six months, net profit increased to RM853 million from RM769 million a year earlier, while revenue rose to RM5.39 billion from RM5.17 billion.
Chief executive officer Goh Seow Eng said the results reflected Maxis' approach of combining steady top-line performance with operating discipline to accelerate profit growth.
He said the company continued to drive margin expansion through focused execution across the business.
"In recognition of these results, the board declared an interim dividend of four sen per share, maintaining our stable dividend payout," he said.
Goh said Maxis' full-year guidance remained unchanged at low single-digit growth in service revenue and Ebitda, with capital expenditure intensity of between 10 per cent and 12 per cent.
"Across the remainder of the year, we remain focused on leveraging our integrated network to create value for consumers and power businesses, while delivering sustainable long-term growth for our shareholders," he said.

Title: Bank Negara expects 5pct GDP growth for 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia remains confident that Malaysia's economy will grow by around five per cent this year, although growth could come in slightly below or above that level.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the economy had continued to perform above expectations over the past three quarters, supported by a broad-based expansion in domestic and external demand.
"We are confident for this year within our range. Most likely it will be around five per cent," he told reporters at a press conference following the release of Malaysia's second-quarter gross domestic produt (GDP) data today.
He said growth remained broad-based, with domestic demand continuing to be the main driver while the external sector provided stronger support in the latest quarter and the previous quarter.
Within exports, both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products recorded growth, while the information and communications technology (ICT) services sector also expanded.
Abdul Rasheed said consumption, investment, exports and tourism were expected to continue supporting economic activity in the second half of the year, although the contribution from individual growth drivers could change amid global uncertainties.
"There will be some adjustments to the drivers of this growth as well," he said.
He said risks to the outlook remained balanced, with a de-escalation of the Middle East conflict, sustained E&E demand and stronger tourism activity presenting potential upside risks.
On the downside, a prolonged Middle East conflict and lower-than-expected production could weigh on growth.
Abdul Rasheed said the central bank did not see the economy overheating despite the strong performance recorded over the past three quarters.
"We don't see excessive demand pressure. Demand is steady, resilient, but it is not excessive," he said.
He said the central bank would continue to monitor developments and assess whether there was a need to revise its growth forecast.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CelcomDigi Q2 net profit falls 9.3pct on higher costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd's net profit fell 9.3 per cent year-on-year to RM398 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, due to increased costs related to 5G network utilisation and net financing.
Quarterly revenue, however, edged up 0.3 per cent to RM3.19 billion from RM3.18 billion, driven by targeted marketing initiatives across its postpaid and home fibre segments.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the initiatives lifted subscriber numbers by 3.8 per cent and 37.2 per cent, respectively, contributing a combined RM61 million to revenue growth.
The gains were partly offset by a RM31 million decline in prepaid revenue, reflecting the group's strategic shift away from single-use prepaid SIM acquisitions, as well as a RM24 million decline in device sales.
For the first half of 2026, net profit slipped 0.9 per cent to RM816 million from RM823 million a year earlier, while revenue was largely unchanged at RM6.39 billion.
The group ended the quarter with 20.3 million subscribers and declared a second interim dividend of 3.4 sen per share.
Chief executive officer Albern Murty said CelcomDigi remained focused on sustainable growth, operational efficiency and long-term value creation.
"We are delivering our operational excellence programmes as planned, generating tangible savings and improving how we operate.
"This enables us to continue investing in priority areas, while sustaining healthy service revenue growth.
"As we move beyond integration, we remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and strategic investments in our network, digital capabilities, and customer experience," he said.
For the second half, CelcomDigi expects to deliver on its full-year operational efficiency targets and begin addressing medium- to longer-term structural costs.
The group is also targeting sustainable service revenue growth and margin improvements, supported by its refreshed product portfolio and focus on individual customer segments.
CelcomDigi said it is working with other Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) shareholders to complete the acquisition of the Finance Ministry's stake in DNB.
Upon completion, its share of DNB's financial results will be accounted for using the equity method, with the acquisition expected to have no impact on its FY26 earnings before interest and tax guidance.
DNB has also embarked on a network modernisation programme using its 240MHz spectrum portfolio, with CelcomDigi expecting to contribute its experience and existing infrastructure to optimise network deployment and costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi insists PM should have attended TH RCI parliamentary sitting
Article:
MARANG: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should have attended the special parliamentary sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
He said this would have allowed Anwar to answer questions raised by members of parliament, and that this was appropriate as Anwar had called for the session.
On Tuesday, Perikatan Nasional MPs requested that the sitting be postponed as Anwar was unable to attend due to medical reasons.
"If we, (opposition), attended, we would only be listening. He (Anwar), must attend and answer," he told reporters after Friday prayers.
He said the prime minister's absence led the opposition to see no need to remain in the hall.
Meanwhile, Hadi expressed confidence that PN would not be suspended by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) following a complaint lodged by Bersatu.
He said there was no evidence or argument showing that the coalition had violated its constitution to warrant such action.
The RoS previously confirmed receiving a complaint from Bersatu, including allegations that the party was excluded from the PN supreme council meeting on July 16, as well as issues concerning its membership status in the coalition.
Hadi also said his statement that Bersatu was no longer part of PN was based on the implied meaning of the party's actions, rather than an interpretation of the coalition's constitution.
He referred to Bersatu's decision to field a candidate against PN in the Negri Sembilan election.
"They fought their own party... what does that mean?" he said.
"What PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar mentioned was from the perspective of the constitution. I spoke from the perspective of its implied meaning."
Samsuri previously said Bersatu's status in PN remained unchanged as no official decision had been made in accordance with the coalition's constitution.

Title: Affin Bank Q2 net profit falls 11pct on higher impairment allowances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Bank Bhd's net profit fell 11.13 per cent year-on-year to RM127.52 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, weighed down by higher impairment allowances and a lower share of profit from associates.
Revenue, however, rose 5.01 per cent to RM647.21 million from RM616.30 million a year earlier, driven by stronger net interest and Islamic banking income, as well as higher fee and commission income.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the banking group said allowance for impairment losses increased by RM38.1 million from a year earlier, while its share of results of associates declined by RM18.4 million.
These were partly offset by RM30.9 million in higher net income and an RM11 million reduction in operating expenses.
Net interest income increased 10.5 per cent to RM235.20 million, while income from Islamic banking business rose 13.9 per cent to RM249.35 million.
Net fee and commission income jumped 60.6 per cent to RM95 million from RM59.16 million. However, net gains on financial instruments fell to RM26.58 million from RM68.61 million, while other income declined to RM41.09 million from RM56.91 million.
Pre-tax profit fell 8.1 per cent to RM165.19 million from RM179.82 million.
Affin's Islamic banking arm's pre-tax profit declined by RM22.7 million to RM75.7 million, mainly due to a RM27 million increase in impairment allowances and RM10.9 million in higher operating expenses.
In contrast, Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd's pre-tax profit more than doubled to RM83.5 million from RM36.7 million, driven mainly by higher fee and commission income and net interest income.
For the first half of 2026, Affin Bank's net profit slipped 1.7 per cent to RM263.02 million from RM267.57 million a year earlier, despite net income rising 12.2 per cent to RM1.30 billion from RM1.16 billion.
The group's loans, advances and financing stood at RM83.07 billion as at end-June, up from RM78.55 billion at end-December 2025. Gross impaired loans, meanwhile, increased to RM1.53 billion from RM1.30 billion.
Cash and short-term funds stood at RM4.87 billion, down from RM6.16 billion at end-2025, while total assets increased to RM129.40 billion from RM124.07 billion.
Total liabilities rose to RM117.02 billion from RM111.85 billion, with deposits from customers at RM78.53 billion compared with RM79 billion at end-2025. Borrowings and sukuk increased to RM7.65 billion from RM6.13 billion.
Affin Bank did not propose a dividend for the financial period under review. It had paid a single-tier final dividend of 8.53 sen per share, amounting to RM216.14 million, for the 2025 financial year on June 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vietjet Thailand to fly to KL from Bangkok on Oct 9
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vietjet Thailand, the subsidiary of low-cost carrier Vietjet Air, will start flying daily to Kuala Lumpur from Bangkok on Oct 9 using its Boeing B737-8 aircraft.
Vietjet Thailand vice president of commercial and customer service, Pinyot Pibulsonggram said the route is an important part of the airline's regional network expansion and will strengthen Bangkok's role as a connecting point for Malaysian travellers wanting to fly to Thailand and the region.
"Our focus is on building sustainable demand in both directions by working closely with the Tourism Authority of Thailand, Tourism Malaysia, travel agents, and our industry partners to drive stronger travel flows between the two countries," he said in a recent statement.
Vietjet Thailand will fly to Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA T2) from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport.
The new route will be the carrier's first direct service to Malaysia. Its first international route using the B737-8 aircraft was to Nha Trang from Bangkok on Jan 29.
Vietjet Thailand said the new service will also connect travellers from Malaysia to its domestic and international network.
The airline added that it is expanding its international network across  Asia Pacific from Thailand to Japan, China, Vietnam, Taipei, Cambodia, India and South Korea, to name a few.
Currently, Vietjet Thailand is operating 12 domestic routes from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi to Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Phuket, Krabi, Udon Thani, Hat Yai, Khon Kaen, Ubon Ratchathani, Nakhon Si Thammarat and Surat Thani, as well as cross-regional flights including from Phuket to Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai.

Title: Loke challenges ECRL to start operations this December
Article:
GOMBAK: Transport Minister Anthony Loke has challenged Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) to bring forward the East Coast Rail Link's opening to early December 2026, ahead of the previously targeted January 2027.
He said the new target was chosen to coincide with year-end school holidays, when many Malaysians travel.
This marks an upgrade on Loke's earlier benchmark, when he said that East Coast residents in the Klang Valley would be able to use the
ECRL in January 2027
.
The System Integration Test and Final Functional Review mark key pre-operational stages for the ECRL, with the Final Functional Review regulated by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD).
"The Transport Ministry is targeting early December 2026, in conjunction with the year-end school holidays and for many of our citizens as well," Loke said at the launch of the Comprehensive Inspection Train and the start of the System Integration Test and Final Functional Review.
He said the ministry was in talks with the Land Public Transport Agency to simplify the Final Functional Review process, which he described as having been rigid.
"The trains had already undergone extensive testing at their factory in China before shipment.
"If this process can be simplified, I want to throw down a challenge to MRL and CCCC to rise to it," he said, addressing MRL chief executive Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak directly.
He repeated the challenge in Mandarin to CCCC representatives, calling an earlier opening a great gift for the Malaysian people.
Loke said any simplification of the approval process would not come at the expense of safety.
"We are more afraid than you are if there is any risk.
"So we will certainly take every consideration into account," he said, when asked whether shortening the process posed any risk.
The Final Functional Review typically takes two to three months, during which trains operate on the line without carrying passengers, and can only begin once all earlier tests have been passed.
Loke said every train set, not just those already delivered, must pass the Final Functional Review before the line can begin commercial operations.
Five sets have arrived in Malaysia so far, with the rest due in the coming months.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CIMB cuts LPI forecasts, target price as underwriting outlook weakens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has cut its earnings forecasts for LPI Capital Bhd by 12.1 per cent to 14 per cent for financial years 2026 to 2028 (FY26-FY28).
The firm cited weaker motor underwriting performance and slower gross written premium (GWP) growth.
CIMB Securities raised its motor portfolio combined ratio assumption to about 100 per cent for FY26-FY28 from 90 per cent previously, reflecting adverse claims experience.
It also lowered its GWP growth forecasts to 6.8 per cent, 6.7 per cent and 6.9 per cent for FY26, FY27 and FY28, respectively, from 8.2 per cent, 8.4 per cent and 7.8 per cent previously.
CIMB Securities said the revisions followed LPI's subdued first-half FY26 GWP growth of 4.1 per cent year-on-year, broadly in line with lacklustre industry growth of 1.4 per cent.
It attributed the slower expansion to the completion of multi-year infrastructure projects and a slower rollout of new large-scale projects ahead of the upcoming general election.
The firm maintained its "Hold" call on LPI but lowered its target price to RM13.30 from RM14.30, based on a FY26 forecast price-to-book value of 2.73 times versus 3.31 times previously.
CIMB Securities said the lower valuation multiple reflected the earnings downgrades and weaker sustainable return on equity following higher-than-expected motor claims.
LPI's first-half FY26 core net profit fell 8.1 per cent year-on-year to RM166.4 million, coming in 6 per cent below CIMB Securities' forecast and 11 per cent below consensus.
The weaker performance was mainly due to higher motor claims, with the portfolio's claims ratio rising to 77 per cent in the second quarter of FY26 from 69 per cent a year earlier.
Investment fair value losses and weaker performance in miscellaneous insurance also weighed on earnings.
The motor portfolio swung to an insurance service loss of RM5.9 million in the first half, from an insurance service result of RM28 million previously.
This offset a 46 per cent increase in insurance service result from the fire underwriting segment.
Meanwhile, Lonpac Insurance's general insurance business recorded a 9.9 per cent decline in pre-tax profit to RM189.2 million, while the investment holding segment's pre-tax profit rose 13 per cent to RM20.8 million on higher dividend income.
CIMB Securities said near- to medium-term earnings could receive support from cross-selling synergies under LPI's bancassurance arrangement with Public Bank, alongside selective expansion in the fire, motor and miscellaneous segments.
However, LPI's strong fire franchise, defensive earnings profile and capital returns following the disposal of its Public Bank stake are likely to be offset by a more challenging underwriting environment.
"With a sizeable equity income buffer progressively removed following the disposal of the Public Bank stake, LPI's investment thesis increasingly hinges on the strength of its general insurance underwriting franchise," it said.
CIMB Securities said a sustained recovery in motor underwriting profitability would be crucial for a meaningful earnings and valuation re-rating.
It identified persistently elevated motor claims severity and higher repair and replacement costs as key downside risks.
Better-than-expected cross-selling synergies with Public Bank, however, could provide upside.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel reopens West Bank settlement evacuated 20 years ago
Article:
GANIM, Palestinian Territories: Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government's policy of rapid settlement expansion.
The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim's new and only street, where future residents and their families – who had come to help with the move – smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.
"A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We're arriving now," new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.
In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.
Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government's policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.
"I'm happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly," he said.
Berkovitch's mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.
"Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever," Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.
Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon's disengagement plan in 2005.
The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.
Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities – Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.
In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.
About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.
"The era of evacuation is over – from here, we only build," Dagan said.
In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim's construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.
On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.
Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.
Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Why investors must look beyond the numbers
Article:
THE eFishery case is a timely reminder that even established safeguards can fail when the information beneath them is deliberately manipulated.
Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (KWAP) invested RM163.4 million in the Indonesian aquaculture technology company, while other major global institutional investors were similarly affected.
According to KWAP's official clarification, the wider case involved deliberate financial manipulation and misrepresentation of the company's financial reporting.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has since cautioned that even verification by renowned international audit firms offers no guarantee.
Reports have also indicated that part of the verification process was not completed in time.
The larger lesson is therefore not simply whether a prescribed process was followed, but whether the evidence underlying an investment has been independently and sufficiently verified.
Beyond The Financials
Financial due diligence remains indispensable. It tests performance, cash flow, financial position and projected returns.
But it largely examines the financial records and information presented to the investor.
In sophisticated fraud, those records may appear consistent while the customers, contracts, transactions, assets or operations behind them are not.
The answer is not less financial scrutiny, but broader scrutiny. Qualitative research should complement quantitative analysis by testing whether the business itself operates as represented.
This means independently verifying key customer relationships and contracts, examining banking arrangements and cash flows, validating operational data, and conducting deeper background checks on founders and senior management.
It also means testing the investment thesis itself: will the business process and model remain relevant over the next five to 10 years?
If a high valuation is being presented, is it supported by the balance sheet, underlying assets and operating evidence? Do those assets actually exist and can they be authenticated?
Behaviour during the investment process can also be revealing.
Unreasonable pressure from either the investor or investee for an immediate decision should be treated as a warning sign that warrants deeper scrutiny, not faster approval.
Verifying The Business Behind The Numbers
The purpose of qualitative due diligence is not simply to collect more documents.
Several documents may repeat the same information without providing genuinely independent confirmation.
Investors must establish where evidence originated, whether it can be authenticated, and whether financial and non-financial information corroborate one another.
For overseas investments, this may require confirmation and authentication with relevant local authorities in the country concerned.
Material discrepancies, whether financial or non-financial, should be investigated and escalated rather than absorbed into an otherwise attractive investment case.
There is also an opportunity to better use external research capability.
Universities can serve as platforms that bridge academic research outcomes with current industry needs, translating research into evidence that can inform investment decisions.
Management and Science University (MSU), for example, has recently expanded industry-academia collaboration through partnerships such as its memorandum with the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing.
Governance requires the same depth of scrutiny. A review should confirm the existence and standing of the company while also assessing the effectiveness of its board in practice.
The combination and representation of board members should be examined to determine whether the business is sufficiently safeguarded.
Board papers around key decisions should also be reviewed for gaps or discrepancies, including whether concerns raised by directors were subsequently addressed by senior management.
How an organisation responds when challenged ultimately portrays its values.
Due Diligence Cannot Stop At Approval
Institutional investors must retain independent judgement even when major international audit firms, advisers or global co-investors are involved.
Investment committees should assess the combined financial and non-financial evidence, not simply whether the prescribed process was completed.
Where concerns remain but can be resolved, an investment may proceed subject to clear conditions and further verification.
If subsequent verification fails to resolve those concerns, the institution must retain the ability to withdraw.
That discipline must continue after capital is deployed. Structured periodic reviews should be implemented before and after investment.
For higher-risk investments involving more complex verification, particularly in areas such as technology and AI, a dedicated committee should continuously monitor and oversee the investment, identify emerging risks and determine when conditions need to change or exposure should be reduced.
Auditors remain an essential line of defence. International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB)'s revised International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 240 strengthens the fraud lens in audit risk assessment and response, but no audit should be treated as a substitute for an investor's own verification.
Credibility in due diligence and financial reporting is a must. But institutions must go beyond the report itself to test the substance and evidence beneath it, with rigorous governance and periodic verification before and after investment.
For institutions entrusted with retirement, public or beneficiary capital, that is not an additional layer of caution.
It is part of responsible stewardship.
*The writer is the president of Malaysian Management Accountants Association.

Title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill two including senior policeman
Article:
GAZA CITY: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed two people including a senior police officer on Thursday, health officials said, the second straight day of bombardment after a lull due to a US peace push.
The Israeli military said it struck a Hamas commander in the Khan Yunis area who it said had been planning attacks against troops, in the second such targeting in as many days.
"The fighter was struck in an aerial strike in order to remove the threat to IDF troops," the military said, adding that "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians."
Gaza's civil defence agency, which operates as a rescue service under Hamas, said an airstrike west of Khan Yunis killed one person, with the city's Nasser Hospital confirming the arrival of a body following the attack.
In a separate incident in Gaza City, the civil defence said one person was killed and several others injured in an Israeli strike on a vehicle in the Sheikh Ajlin neighbourhood.
Al-Shifa Hospital said it had received the body of Gaza City's police governor Jamal Abu Kamil.
Gaza's interior ministry confirmed Abu Kamil "was assassinated in an Israeli airstrike targeting his vehicle on Al-Rashid Street, southwest of Gaza City."
The Israeli military confirmed the killing, and said in a statement that Abu Kamil was "a commander in the Hamas  organisation who infiltrated Israeli territory" during the group's attack on Oct 7, 2023, which sparked the most recent war in Gaza.
It said throughout the war Abu Kamil had "advanced attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians."
Hamas issued a condemnation, saying in a statement that Abu Kamil's killing constituted a "further escalation of the brutal crimes" committed by Israel, and calling on mediating countries to force Israel to halt its "violations" of the ceasefire.
On Wednesday, Israel carried out its first airstrike in Gaza since August 3.
The hiatus in airstrikes came after US President Donald Trump's announcement of a "major milestone" in his plan to end the war.
Hamas had announced that it would disarm by giving its weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee.
Trump's "Board of Peace", in charge of implementing the ceasefire deal, had initially announced that Israel in turn would start a phased withdrawal from much of the Gaza Strip.
But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday publicly rejected the deal and vowed no Israeli pullout, even after the Board of Peace reassured him that Israel would not have to withdraw until complete Hamas disarmament.
Israeli operations in Gaza have killed 1,260 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Makkah defence pact should be viewed in the right context
Article:
LETTERS:
Many analyses of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan begin by asking whether the Muslim world is creating an "Islamic Nato''?
The more important question is whether it could mark the beginning of a greater strategic autonomy for the Muslim world — the ability to develop their own security capabilities, technologies and diplomatic leverage without remaining dependent on major powers.
If the agreement simply creates another military bloc, the Muslim world is not creating anything fundamentally new. It is only reproducing the security structures that major powers have built.
This is where we need to distinguish between a symbolic ummah and a strategic ummah. A symbolic ummah is strong in the language of solidarity. We see declarations, emergency meetings, conferences and statements of support whenever a major crisis affects Muslim societies.
A strategic ummah requires the ability to turn solidarity into capacity, technology, diplomacy, economic influence and strategic leverage.
Palestine becomes the moral and semiotic axis of this distinction. This, however, does not mean that Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan must go to war with Israel.
Strategic power can also mean diplomatic and economic pressure, humanitarian assistance, reconstruction, influence in international institutions and stronger bargaining power for the Palestinians. But Palestine is not the only test. Security must be understood more broadly.
Security in the Muslim world must also include human security, food, energy, technology, maritime routes, cybersecurity, refugees and the protection of vulnerable communities affected by conflict.
Plus, the Makkah Agreement could benefit Washington. If regional countries become more capable of defending themselves, the US may be able to reduce some of its security burden in the region. If the agreement also helps balance Iran, it may align with some American strategic interests.
The real test of autonomy will come when the interests of the Makkah Agreement countries no longer align with Washington. Collective security is relatively easy to declare; it becomes much harder when fulfilling that commitment carries diplomatic, economic or military costs.
This is also where the idea of a strategic ummah will face its strongest test. If the agreement works only when its actions remain acceptable to Washington or other Western capitals, then it cannot yet be described as an independent security architecture.
The Makkah Agreement, therefore, should not be measured by whether it can become an alternative to Nato as there is no need for an "Islamic Nato" at all.
What it needs is the ability to define for itself what security means, who should be protected, and what its power should ultimately be used for.
ISMAIL HASHIM YAHAYA
Former lecturer,
Universiti Selangor

Title: No time limit on Nurul Izzah's leave, says Fuziah
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR has not set a time limit for deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar's leave of absence, which begins next week as she resumes her studies.
Its secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the party would give Nurul Izzah as much time as she needed, stressing that pursuing her studies was equally important after years of commitment to the party.
She said PKR was ready to welcome Nurul Izzah back as deputy president once she was ready to resume her duties.
"So far, we have not imposed any time limit on the deputy president's leave as she wants to continue her studies.
"InsyaAllah, we are ready to welcome her back when she is ready to resume her duties," she said during a press conference after attending the opening of the 2026 PKR Wanita and Youth national congresses at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
Fuziah said Nurul Izzah would first complete her responsibilities throughout the PKR national congress before beginning her leave.
Meanwhile, Fuziah said representatives from 25 foreign embassies had confirmed their attendance at the congress tomorrow.
She added that delegates would debate five motions, comprising the motion on the president's policy speech and four motions proposed by the central leadership council covering the economy and political stability, health, national unity and strengthening the party.

Title: Police probe claim 12-year-old boy chased by Hilux in Pasir Gudang
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: Police are investigating a claim that a 12-year-old boy was followed and chased by a Toyota Hilux while walking home from school in Taman Megah Ria here on Tuesday.
The boy's father, a trader, claimed in a post on his Threads account, chompchomp_pasta, that the incident occurred while his son and his friends were walking home.
"My son encountered a Hilux that was slowly following him and his friends from behind, from the multipurpose hall until the area near the Taman Megah Ria mosque.
"My son became worried and asked all his friends to run and split up.
"However, the Hilux chased my son and made two rounds while chasing him. Fortunately, a nasi campur trader in front of a house called out to my son," he said.
He said the woman asked his son to come closer and sit with her.
"However, the Hilux then stopped near the woman's house.
"A man and his family members also came out of the house before the Hilux left," he said.
The father said his son then contacted his mother and asked her to come to the location.
"He asked for the trader's mobile phone before I received a call from my wife informing me about the incident.
"At the time, I was working," he said.
He added that the trader told his wife that two girls had previously also been targeted by a black Hilux and that she had helped them.
"When I asked my son whether he saw anyone inside the Hilux, he said there was a woman wearing a headscarf and sunglasses.
"However, he said the area beside the woman's seat was dark.
"My son said the woman took photographs of him and his friend.
"As he was panicking, my son did not see the vehicle's registration number," he said.
The father urged parents and members of the public to remain vigilant when children were returning home from school.
Meanwhile, Seri Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Sohaimi Ishak said police received a report from the boy at 4.45pm on Tuesday.
"The boy claimed that he was followed by a vehicle in the Seri Alam area.
"At the same time, police became aware of the incident after it was uploaded on Threads by the owner of the chompchomp_pasta account.
"Seri Alam police take this incident seriously and are conducting further investigations, including identifying witnesses and determining the motive behind the incident," he said in a statement today.
He said monitoring in the area had also been stepped up to ensure the safety and wellbeing of residents.
"Those with information about the incident can contact the nearest police station or the Seri Alam district control centre at 07-3871422 or the hotline at 07-3861422," he said.

Title: Man held over BMW fire linked to money-lending arrangement in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 22-year-old man, believed to be a moneylender's runner, has been remanded for seven days over an attack in which a BMW was set on fire in Air Itam.
The remand order was issued by magistrate Noor Idayu Salim and began today to facilitate police investigations under Section 435 of the Penal Code.
The suspect is believed to have been paid between RM900 and RM1,000 to set fire to a BMW 220i belonging to a 61-year-old man at Jalan RU3 Air Itam on Aug 8.
Preliminary investigations found that the incident was allegedly linked to a RM6,000 money-lending arrangement taken out by the victim's son after he saw a loan advertisement on Facebook on Aug 5.
The incident caused the victim an estimated RM40,000 in losses.
Acting on information, police arrested the suspect at Taman Sejahtera, Bukit Mertajam, yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak plans RM50mil regenerative medicine hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak is proposing a RM50 million investment to develop Southeast Asia's first integrated regenerative medicine hub, aimed at bringing research, manufacturing and clinical applications under one roof.
The Sarawak Regenerative BioFoundry is a collaboration between Malaysian Bioeconomy Development Corp and BioVerde Technologies Sdn Bhd, the commercial arm of the Sarawak Biodiversity Council.
Located at the Sarawak Bioindustrial Park, the facility will support the development of cell and gene therapy products, which use living cells or genetic material to treat complex diseases, including certain cancers and genetic disorders.
Bioeconomy Corp said the BioFoundry would help accelerate regenerative medicine innovations from the laboratory to patients, while supporting the production and supply of the products to hospitals and clinical partners in Sarawak and the wider region.
Its chief executive officer Mohd Khairul Fidzal Abdul Razak said Malaysia needed stronger infrastructure and clearer development pathways to translate healthcare research into treatments for patients.
"Cell and gene therapy is still an emerging field in Malaysia. Although local biotechnology companies are developing promising technologies, many continue to face challenges in securing clinical validation and bringing their products to market," he said in a statement.
Mohd Khairul said Bioeconomy Corp currently supports biotechnology companies developing more than 50 cell and gene therapy products, providing a potential pipeline for the BioFoundry.
He said the facility would give companies in Bioeconomy Corp's ecosystem a platform to test, validate and advance their technologies in a healthcare environment.
The BioFoundry will comprise four components covering manufacturing, clinical activities, technology and research, and wellness, and will operate in accordance with Health Ministry guidelines and regulatory requirements.
Under the collaboration, Bioeconomy Corp and BioVerde will jointly develop these activities and facilitate engagement with healthcare regulators, as well as support talent development and access to incentives.
BioVerde chief executive officer Hazwan Razak said the BioFoundry would help catalyse high-value industries at the Sarawak Bioindustrial Park by connecting research, manufacturing, clinical applications and investment.
The initiative is also expected to support Sarawak's economic diversification by attracting investment, creating high-skilled jobs and strengthening its biotechnology and healthcare ecosystem.
The collaboration builds on a memorandum of understanding signed between Bioeconomy Corp and BioVerde in October 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Magna Prima sets out RM700mil 8 Conlay rehabilitation deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Magna Prima Bhd's proposed restructuring and rehabilitation of the troubled 8 Conlay development involves a commercial entitlement of up to RM700 million, to be satisfied through redeemable secured loan securities (RSLS).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Magna Prima said the RM700 million represents the agreed commercial allocation arising from the transfer of the development undertaking to Delta 8 Sdn Bhd, the special purpose vehicle set up for the restructuring.
The arrangement also involves the assumption of specified liabilities by Magna Prima's wholly owned subsidiary Permata Juang (M) Sdn Bhd.
Magna Prima stressed that the RM700 million is not the purchase price of the land or the development undertaking.
Instead, the entitlement will be satisfied through various classes of RSLS under a rehabilitation agreement between Permata Juang, Damai City Sdn Bhd and Delta 8.
Damai City, the developer of 8 Conlay, is in liquidation and under receivership.
Magna Prima said the RM700 million entitlement was agreed on a willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, taking into account an independent valuation of the land and buildings forming part of the development.
City Valuers & Consultants Sdn Bhd valued the assets at RM721 million as at June 23, 2025.
The company said its board took into account the RM700 million entitlement being below the independent valuation, as well as the rationale and prospects of the proposed development.
Under the restructuring, Permata Juang will also provide RM70 million in cash to Damai City's solicitors to be held in escrow.
The amount, to be funded through internally generated funds and/or borrowings if required, will be used as an advance redemption payment for the relevant RSLS.
Subject to the fulfilment of conditions and relevant court orders, the restructuring will cover the 8 Conlay development, including its 1.48-hectare freehold site, existing assets, sale and purchase agreements, development rights and arrangements for existing buyers.
The proposed rehabilitation also provides a framework for 564 existing purchasers, comprising 404 units in Tower A and 160 units in Tower B.
Trading in Magna Prima shares was halted this morning following the announcement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police appeal for information on missing Kajang teenager
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking the public's assistance in locating 17-year-old Farzanah Nabila Abdullah, who was reported missing from Taman Jasmin, Kajang, early yesterday.
Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report concerning the girl's disappearance about 1.20pm yesterday.
"She is about 155cm tall, weighs 42kg and has a slim build, with long straight hair and a tan complexion.
"Farzanah was believed to have gone missing at 12.20am yesterday, with her last known location recorded at 940, Jalan Jasmin 28, Taman Jasmin, Kajang," he said in a statement.
He urged anyone with information on her whereabouts to contact the Kajang district police headquarters at 03-8911 4222 or investigating officer Sergeant Amiruddin Abdul Hamid at 013-230 4156.

Title: Rafales, Typhoons, Nato jets converge on Subang Air Base
Article:
SUBANG: Fighter jets, strategic airlifters and aerial tankers from Malaysia, India, Germany, Spain and Nato converged on Subang this week, turning the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base here into a hive of military air activity.
The aircraft are transiting through Subang after participating in Exercise Pitch Black 2026 in Australia, with some also taking part in bilateral training between the RMAF and Indian Air Force (IAF).
Among the aircraft spotted by the New Straits Times were Dassault Rafale fighters and Boeing C-17 Globemaster III strategic transport aircraft from the IAF, Spanish and German Eurofighter Typhoons, and Spanish and Nato Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transports (MRTT).
Also present were Airbus A400M Atlas transport aircraft operated by the German and Spanish air forces.
For the IAF, the stopover also coincided with
Exercise Udara Shakti 2026
, a bilateral air exercise with the RMAF that began on Monday to enhance the interoperability of both air forces.
RMAF and IAF fighter aircraft have been taking part in tactical sorties since Tuesday, including Dissimilar Basic Fighter Manoeuvres, Dissimilar Air Combat Training, air-to-air refuelling and aerial photography.
The exercises have given both air forces the opportunity to operate different aircraft types in a complex training environment while testing their coordination, communications, procedures, logistics and ability to make rapid operational decisions.

Title: #NSTviral: Ford Ranger driver criticised over pedestrian crossing footage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Ford Ranger driver has drawn criticism after dashcam footage appeared to show the vehicle continuing through a pedestrian crossing as several people crossed the road.
In the 15-second video, the 4WD was seen approaching the pedestrian crossing while the traffic light was still red.
The vehicle appeared to continue moving as pedestrians made their way across the road.
The footage sparked criticism from social media users, with several calling on the authorities to take action against the driver.
Some commenters urged the Road Transport Department and police to investigate the incident.
One user, @Eldard Low, commented, "It's really embarrassing."
User @Suhaimi Ismail also commented, "When I was in California, US, cars had to stop even if they had the right of way. Pedestrians were given priority."

Title: Malaysia's inflation rises to 1.9pct in Q2 as fuel costs increase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, from 1.6 per cent in the first quarter on higher external cost pressures and rising fuel prices.
Bank Negara Malaysia said the increase was mainly linked to the economic impact of the conflict in the Middle East.
Fuel prices, particularly RON97 and diesel, increased during the quarter, resulting in fuel inflation rising to five per cent compared with a 1.5 per cent decline in the first quarter.
Despite the increase in headline inflation, underlying price pressures moderated.
Core inflation eased to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent in the first quarter, reflecting softer price increases in areas including jewellery and watches and rent.
Inflation in jewellery and watches moderated to 23.7 per cent, from 39.1 per cent previously, while rent inflation eased to 1.4 per cent from 1.6 per cent.
Producer cost pressures also increased during the quarter, although Bank Negara said these pressures remained concentrated at the upstream stage, with limited pass-through to later stages of production and broader consumer prices.
The breadth of price increases widened during the quarter.
The share of Consumer Price Index items recording monthly price increases rose to 45.5 per cent, from 38.3 per cent in the first quarter, broadly in line with its historical average of 45.6 per cent.
The increase was driven mainly by a sharp rise in April before moderating in May and June.
Bank Negara expects inflation to remain moderate in 2026, with headline inflation projected to average between 1.5 per cent and 2.5 per cent.
The central bank said external cost pressures stemming from the Middle East conflict could put some upward pressure on prices, but the overall impact is expected to remain contained.
Targeted fuel subsidies and stable domestic demand are expected to limit the pass-through of higher global costs to consumers.
The outlook for inflation therefore remains relatively benign, although global energy prices and geopolitical developments will remain key risks for the Malaysian economy in the months ahead.

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia's economy grows 6pct in Q2, beats advance estimate [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy expanded 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026), exceeding the 5.8 per cent advance estimate and accelerating from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter.
The stronger performance was supported by resilient domestic spending and solid export growth, with all major economic sectors except agriculture expanding during the quarter, Bank Negara Malaysia said.
On a quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted basis, the economy grew 2.5 per cent in Q2, after a marginal contraction of 0.03 per cent in the previous quarter.
For the first half of 2026, Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent, higher than the 4.5 per cent growth recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said consumer spending remained a key driver of growth, with sustained increases in retail transactions pointing to resilient household spending.
"Household spending is expected to remain well-supported, underpinned by continued improvements in income prospects," he told reporters at a press conference.
Investment activity continued to be supported by foreign investments and a steady pipeline of newly approved projects, particularly in high-value-added manufacturing and services activities such as electrical and electronics (E&E), chemicals and information and communication technology (ICT).
"As of June, 85 per cent of manufacturing projects approved between 2021 and February 2026 had progressed to implementation, ranging from factory construction to production and machinery installation.
"On the external front, exports grew strongly in Q2, supported by broad-based expansion across key export segments," Abdul Rasheed said.
He said E&E exports remained the key driver, reflecting strong external demand amid the ongoing global technology upcycle.
"E&E exports are expected to remain the key driver of our export growth, supporting Malaysia's external sector performance as we go forward," he said.
Abdul Rasheed said Malaysia's diverse export base would continue to support the external sector, while sustained investment in data centres was expected to provide further support to digital services exports.
On the supply side, growth was underpinned by the services and manufacturing sectors, alongside a rebound in mining and quarrying.
The stronger services performance was supported by business-related subsectors, particularly ICT and data centre activities, while manufacturing growth was driven by export-oriented clusters, especially E&E, amid continued demand for artificial intelligence-related components.
The mining sector rebounded on stronger natural gas production, while agriculture contracted as oil palm production normalised following strong yields in 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police hunt 2 women over RM16k gold bracelet theft in Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Police are tracking down two women believed to be involved in the theft of a gold bracelet worth about RM16,000 from a jewellery shop at Batu 8, Kampung Batu Enam, Jalan Kelantan, here, yesterday morning.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the incident occurred at 10.59am yesterday. Police received a report from a sales assistant at the jewellery shop at 10.25pm.
He said the theft was discovered when a shop employee conducted a stock check and found that a 916 gold bracelet weighing 28.01g was missing.
"A check of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed the two women entering the shop, before one of them asked the employee to show her several gold bracelets for comparison.
"The suspect then put one of the bracelets on her wrist before concealing it with her sleeve," he said.
He said the suspect also dropped the bracelet on the floor before stepping on it, then picked it up and put it into her handbag.
"At the same time, the second suspect is believed to have distracted the employee by pointing towards another gold bracelet, causing the employee not to notice her accomplice's actions.
"Both suspects then left the shop on the pretext of getting money to make payment, but did not return," he said.
He said the first suspect was wearing a grey robe, black headscarf and black face veil, while the second suspect was wearing a dark blue robe and a blue floral-patterned headscarf.
"The shop employee can identify the second suspect but could not identify the first as her face was covered by the veil.
"Police are actively tracking down both suspects and the case is being investigated under Section 380 of the Penal Code," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: STT GDC secures RM5.6bil financing for Johor data centre campus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres (STT GDC) has secured a green financing facility of up to US$1.37 billion (RM5.6 billion) to support the development of its flagship Malaysian data centre campus in Johor.
Through the investment, STT GDC is also committed to building local capabilities, strengthening industry partnerships and operating responsibly as it expands in Johor, said the company in a statement today.
STT was established in 2014 as part of Singapore Technologies Telemedia (ST Telemedia), a strategic investment company backed by Temasek Holdings, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund.
The financing package includes a green loan facility for the first phase of the STT Johor campus at Nusa Cemerlang Industrial Park in Iskandar Puteri.
United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd is the sole coordinator and mandated lead arranger for the financing, while OCBC Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia Bhd and CIMB Bank Bhd are the other mandated lead arrangers.
STT GDC group chief financial officer Nelson Lim said the financing marked an important milestone in the company's continued investment in Malaysia.
"It also demonstrates the confidence that its banking partners have in both the project and the long-term outlook for the digital infrastructure sector.
"As demand for cloud, artificial intelligence (AI) and other digital workloads grows, disciplined, long-term capital will be critical to building infrastructure that is resilient, sustainable and able to support our customers' requirements," he said.
Lim said the facility also reinforced STT GDC's approach to incorporating sustainability into the financing, design, construction and operation of its data centres.
The STT Johor campus has a planned development capacity of up to 166 megawatts of information technology load.
It is intended to serve customers requiring scalable digital infrastructure for cloud computing, AI, high-performance computing and other next-generation workloads.
STT GDC said Johor's connectivity, access to power infrastructure, expanding talent pool and proximity to Singapore had strengthened the state's position as a destination for hyperscale and large-scale digital infrastructure investment.
The campus is also expected to support the objectives of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, including greater cross-border economic cooperation and Johor's development as a high-value investment destination.
STT GDC Malaysia country head Darryll Sinnappa said the campus reflected the company's long-term commitment to Malaysia and its confidence in Johor's role as a strategic digital infrastructure hub.
"The campus is being developed to support the next generation of digital infrastructure requirements, including cloud, AI and high-performance computing workloads, while contributing to Malaysia's digital economy ambitions," he said.
In April 2026, the company launched talent and community development initiatives in the state in collaboration with the Johor Talent Development Council, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia and EPI Group.
The programme builds on a memorandum of understanding signed by STT GDC and the council in 2025 to develop a pipeline of skilled professionals for Johor's data centre industry and the wider region.
According to its latest environmental, social and governance report, renewable energy accounted for 83.2 per cent of STT GDC's electricity consumption in 2025.
The company also reduced its carbon intensity by 70.5 per cent from its 2021 baseline, surpassing its 2028 target three years ahead of schedule.
Its average power usage effectiveness stood at 1.44, representing a 13 per cent improvement from the 2020 baseline, while water usage effectiveness improved by 41.2 per cent over the same period.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: My son's case has 'gone quiet and died', says Rafizi a year after attack [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli claims the investigation into the attack on his son in Putrajaya a year ago has "gone quiet and died".
"A year has passed, and the case has simply gone quiet and died," the former Pandan member of parliament said in a video posted on social media.
He claimed he was "informally informed" by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail about a suspected mastermind.
"But when I asked him to answer publicly in Parliament, he declined. An attack like this may be forgotten by the authorities but not by the victim's family."
Recalling the incident on Aug 13 last year, Rafizi said his son, who was 12 at the time, was attacked in public as he was about to enter a car.
"The attacker was dressed in all-black riding gear with a helmet covering his face. He grabbed and wrapped his arm around my son's neck, injecting something into my son's shoulder twice while shouting to my wife, 'I injected him'.
"That night and the following morning, my wife received several WhatsApp messages threatening 'keep quiet, next is HIV'. CCTV footage exists because it happened during the day."
Rafizi claimed the attack was intended to intimidate his wife into forcing him to retire from politics.
The former PKR deputy president said he would continue to mark the date of the incident until those responsible were brought to justice.
Police previously recorded statements from 19 people, while the phone number used to threaten Rafizi's wife was registered under a foreigner's name.
However, the attacker has yet to be identified as the CCTV footage obtained was unclear.
In January, Saifuddin said certain details could not be disclosed to avoid disrupting efforts to track down the suspect and compromising the safety of key witnesses.
He also said the case remained under investigation, adding that any decision to classify it as No Further Action (NFA) would depend on new developments and leads discovered by the police.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ECRL on track to start commercial operations by Jan 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) has reached 95.08 per cent overall progress and entered its testing and commissioning phase ahead of commercial operations in January 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the project remained on schedule for Phase 1 completion in December with the Kota Bharu-Gombak alignment targeted to begin operations in January 2027.
Phase 2, connecting Gombak to Port Klang is expected to be completed by December 2027 with operations scheduled to begin in January 2028.
"Today, the ECRL project has achieved another important milestone through the commissioning of the comprehensive inspection train (CIT), an advanced and high-technology train to be used for inspection and maintenance of the 665-kilometre ECRL network," he said in his keynote address.
Loke said electricity activation had also been completed at all 10 feeder stations along the Kota Bharu-Gombak alignment three days ago.
The project has now shifted its focus towards integrating various railway systems and conducting testing and commissioning to ensure safe and reliable operations.
System integration testing (SIT) will assess the integration of railway infrastructure systems, followed by fault-free run (FFR) testing in September to evaluate passenger electric multiple units (EMUs) and electric locomotives (E-Locos) for cargo operations.
The first six-car EMU and E-Loco will each undergo an 8,000-kilometre FFR under the supervision of the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD).
The six-car EMU, manufactured by CRRC Dalian can record track geometry parameters, inspect railway signalling systems and examine the electrical flow of the Overhead Catenary System.
The train could operate at speeds of up to 160 km/h and was equipped with a control room, conference room, prayer room, dining area, business class cabin, multimedia room and washroom.
He said the CIT had completed assembly and successfully passed its factory acceptance test as scheduled and was expected to arrive in Malaysia on Aug 16.
The CIT will subsequently conduct comprehensive inspections along the ECRL alignment to support the project's operation and maintenance phase.
"The ECRL train will shorten passenger travel time and connect the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station with KotaSAS Station in just 1 hour 35 minutes via the express route, compared with about three hours by road.
"Meanwhile, travel time by ECRL from Gombak to Kuala Terengganu will take about three hours, while the journey from Gombak to Kota Bharu is estimated at only four hours," said Loke.
While the first phase of the ECRL between Kota Bharu and Gombak  is scheduled to start operations in January 2027, Loke has thrown in a challenge to Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) for the project to be opened earlier than scheduled.
The ECRL would have the capacity to carry up to about 10,000 passengers a day during its initial operations.
Loke said the project would have 10 train sets with each set capable of carrying between 300 and 425 passengers, depending on the configuration.
"If one train set makes two to three trips a day, we estimate the capacity could reach about 10,000 passengers a day," he said.
He added currently five ECRL train sets had so far arrived in Malaysia, with the remaining sets expected to arrive over the coming months
During Friday's launching of the CIT, MRL has also unveiled designs for its main stations, incorporating local heritage, architecture and cultural elements from Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor.
Loke said the Gombak station had reached 98.96 per cent construction progress and was expected to be completed in September 2026.
Built on 9.96 hectares, the station will feature elevated platforms, passenger waiting areas, a Business Class Lounge, convenience stores, parking facilities and covered walkways.
The station will also connect with the Kelana Jaya LRT Line and the 24-hour Gombak Integrated Terminal, strengthening connectivity between the ECRL and existing public transport networks.
"With the encouraging progress of the ECRL project, I believe the people's wait to enjoy the ECRL service will become a reality as scheduled, and East Coast residents will be able to return to their hometowns to celebrate Aidilfitri by taking the ECRL in 2027," he said.

Title: Pakistani man pleads guilty to robbery, causing hurt over mobile phone
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A Pakistani man pleaded guilty in the Sessions Court here today to robbing and causing hurt to a man over a mobile phone.
Muhammad Zeeshan Akbar, 24, entered the plea after the charge was read in English before judge Juraidah Abbas.
He nodded to indicate he understood the charge and penalty.
"Plead guilty," he told the court.
Zeeshan admitted to robbing and intentionally causing hurt to Teh Jiann Zhao in an incident involving an Oppo Find N5 mobile phone at Block 17, Taman Batu Bukit Flats, Tanjung Tokong, about 10pm on Aug 5.
The charge was framed under Section 394 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Anuarul Hakim Abdul Muen appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
Anuarul told the court no bail was offered as the accused was a foreigner.
"The accused also does not have valid travel documents," he said.
Juraidah then fixed Sept 14 for the prosecution to present the facts and for the court to determine the sentence, as well as for the accused to engage a lawyer.
"No bail is offered," she told the accused.
It is understood that the accused allegedly posed as a buyer in a cash-on-delivery (COD) phone transaction before assaulting the victim and fleeing with the mobile phone.
The 31-year-old victim is believed to have sustained facial injuries in the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor DAP delegates free to decide on unity government position
Article:
KULAI: Johor DAP will give its delegates the freedom to decide whether the party should remain in the unity government at its congress this Sunday.
Its chairman, Teo Nie Ching said the party would abide by whatever decision was reached through a vote by delegates at the congress.
She said Johor DAP had yet to take a position on the matter as the decision would be determined through a vote.
"Actually, we do not have a position at the state level yet because it involves a vote. We will give delegates the freedom to decide at Sunday's congress.
"It is up to them. Yesterday, we held a dialogue session with the secretary-general (Anthony Loke) to explain the motion.
"Johor will abide by the decision made on Sunday," she told reporters after handing over an allocation under the 2026 Madani Adopted Schools programme by the Communications Ministry at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Murni Jaya in Kampung Murni Jaya, Layang-Layang, here today.
The deputy communications minister said party leaders were confident that delegates would make the best decision for the future direction of the party and the country.
She said delegates were not asked to declare their positions during the dialogue session, but were instead allowed to raise questions about the party's direction and express their views.
"Johor is one of the states with a relatively large number of delegates. I believe they are capable of representing their respective branches at the congress because they understand the party's struggle and principles.
"So, I believe they will make the best decision for the future direction of the party and the country," she said.
Meanwhile, when asked to comment on a political analyst's claim that 14 Pakatan Harapan seats would fall within the red and yellow zones should Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional unite, the Kulai MP said DAP would do its best to defend its seats.
"Thank you for the analysis. We will do our best to face the next general election and defend our seats. We are prepared to face any situation," she said.
Earlier, Teo handed over RM100,000 in allocation to SK Murni Jaya, which was selected as one of the Madani Adopted Schools to carry out various facility upgrades.
The allocation will be used to provide two interactive smartboards, improve lighting and the school's overall appearance, install a public address system in the hall, provide two air-conditioning units, 10 iPads, a Sumo robot set and two smart televisions for the Integrated Special Education Programme classrooms.
The allocation will also cover improvements to the preschool garden, benefiting 189 pupils at the school. All projects are expected to be completed by October.
