Title: Teo Nie Ching insists Johor DAP won’t dictate, delegates hold Cabinet fate in Sunday congress
Article:
KULAI, Aug 14 — Johor DAP delegates are free to decide whether the party’s leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of the special congress this Sunday.
Johor DAP chief Teo Nie Ching said the state leadership is leaving it to more than 400 delegates, who have the freedom to make decisions based on their respective views and understanding of the party’s direction.
“In Johor, the state party does not have a single position or stance on the matter. We give the freedom to the delegates or representatives to make that decision at DAP’s national congress this Sunday.
“Johor DAP even held a dialogue session yesterday with party’s secretary-general Anthony Loke to explain the issue.
“Regardless of the session, the party’s state leadership chose to give delegates the freedom to make their own decisions,” she told reporters after attending an allocation handover event at Sekolah Kebangsaan Murni Jaya here today.
Teo, who is also the DAP’s national vice chairman, was responding to media queries on the party’s Johor state decision ahead of the national congress that is expected to determine whether the party should remain in the government.
It was previously reported that a motion on the decision would be tabled by more than 4,000 delegates at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) in Putrajaya.
Teo, who is also the Kulai MP, said that Johor DAP would accept and abide by any decision made at the congress.
She said Johor is one of the states with a fairly high representation among delegates attending.
“I believe there are members who can represent their respective branches and understand the situation based on the party’s struggle and principles.
“I am of the opinion that they will make the right call based on the party’s direction and the country,” she said.
DAP’s congress this Sunday at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) is expected to focus on the party’s position in the federal unity government.
The congress comes amid growing debate over slow reforms and electoral setbacks within the party, including whether it should remain part of the administration under Anwar.

Title: Malaysia’s inflation outlook steady at 1.5–2.5 pc, BNM stresses external pressures remain manageable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia’s headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 1.6 per cent in the preceding quarter, while core inflation moderated to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said today.
BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said higher input costs had so far seen limited pass through to consumer prices.
He noted that almost 80 per cent of firms are facing higher cost pressures, but only about half indicated they may pass these costs on to consumers, as demand remains weak.
The central bank’s figures showed producer cost pressures were concentrated at the upstream stage, with crude materials prices rising 27.5 per cent and intermediate inputs 3.7 per cent, while finished goods prices increased 1.4 per cent.
Headline inflation is projected to average 1.5 to 2.5 per cent in 2026, with BNM saying the overall impact of external cost pressures is expected to remain contained.
MORE TO COME

Title: One year after son attacked, Rafizi decries threats, says case ‘died off’ unresolved
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — After a year since the attack on his child in Putrajaya, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has claimed the case has “gone quiet and died off”.
“A year has passed, and the case has gone quiet,” he wrote on Facebook, adding that he had been informally told by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail of a suspected mastermind, but his request for an open statement in Parliament was rejected.
He stressed that such an attack was unprecedented in Malaysia. “Never before has a child been assaulted and a wife threatened simply because of her husband’s political stance,” he said.
Rafizi claimed the assault was intended to pressure his wife into forcing him to retire from politics. He thanked his family for standing firm, saying: “If I bowed to such threats, I would be complicit in allowing wrongdoing, damage and crime to continue in this country.”
He warned that if such methods could be used against the child of a former minister, ordinary citizens could face similar intimidation.
Rafizi vowed to continue seeking justice. “I will wait for 13 August every year until the attacker and those behind them are brought to justice. Even if the authorities do not act, I know they will have to answer in the hereafter,” he said.
Recalling the incident on August 13 last year, Rafizi said his child was attacked in public while attempting to enter a car. He recounted that the assailant, dressed in dark rider’s clothing and wearing a helmet, grabbed his child by the neck and injected him twice in the shoulder while shouting at his wife. He added that his wife later received WhatsApp messages threatening that “the next would be HIV.”
In January, Saifuddin Nasution stated that certain information could not be disclosed to avoid jeopardising investigations or witness safety, adding that the case remained under probe pending new leads.

Title: Landfill lunches? Sabah group asks Kota Kinabalu City Hall to clarify packed food claims
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — The Sabah Environment Action Group (SEAG) is seeking a clarification from City Hall (DBKK) over claims that food vendors are selling packed meals at the Kayu Madang landfill.
This follows a social media post circulated widely, which prompted members of the public to reach out to SEAG for clarity on the matter.
The post, which appeared on the Instagram page sabah.info, suggested that food vendors were selling packed food at the landfill and asked whether anyone wished to place an order.
In a statement Thursday, SEAG hoped City Hall could clarify whether this was indeed taking place at the municipal landfill, located in the KKIP area, which serves not only Kota Kinabalu but also neighbouring municipalities, including Petagas, Putatan, Penampang, Tuaran and Kota Belud.
The group noted that from a public health perspective, such activity would raise concerns given the hygiene conditions typically associated with landfill sites.
It added that because the landfill serves multiple municipalities, identifying the source of any potential health issue could prove challenging, which underscored the importance of addressing the matter early.
The group said they will formally write to the DBKK to verify the claims and, should they be substantiated, to encourage appropriate measures and awareness efforts for food vendors, City Hall staff and others at the site regarding food safety and hygiene practices. — Daily Express

Title: Malaysia’s economy expands 6pc in Q2, first‑half growth steady at 5.7pc, says BNM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, AUG 14 — Malaysia’s economy expanded by 6 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.
Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said growth remained broad-based, supported by domestic demand and strong export performance.
“Both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E exports were growing, alongside support from ICT services,” Abdul Rasheed told a joint press conference here today.
The services sector grew 5.9 per cent, manufacturing 7.3 per cent, mining and quarrying 9.2 per cent, and construction 6.5 per cent, while agriculture contracted 3.7 per cent.
Private consumption increased 4.8 per cent, while private investment rose 4.3 per cent.
Abdul Rasheed said growth for the full year was expected to be around 5 per cent, although BNM would retain its existing 4 to 5 per cent forecast range for now.
MORE TO COME

Title: In Johor, police probe claim of suspected Toyota Hilux following student walking home
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — Police are investigating a report that a Toyota Hilux followed a food trader’s 12-year-old son as he was walking home in Taman Megah Ria here on Tuesday.
Seri Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Sohaimi Ishak today said police were actively investigating the alleged incident involving the primary school pupil, which was reported to have occurred at 4.45pm.
“In the report, the boy claimed to be followed by the Toyota Hilux in the Seri Alam area.
“At the same time, police were also despatched to the location of the incident shortly after the victim’s parent uploaded his son’s ordeal on Threads.
“The Seri Alam police is taking this incident seriously and is currently identifying witnesses and the motive for the incident,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Sohaimi said police were also monitoring the Taman Megah Ria area to enhance safety and security following the report.
He advised the public to refrain from speculation and spreading unverified information related to the case.
Yesterday, a Threads user identified as @chompchomp_pasta posted about the incident, warning residents about a Toyota Hilux he claimed had followed his son in the Taman Megah Ria residential area.
He claimed his son was walking home with a friend when they were followed by unknown individuals in a black Toyota Hilux.
The boy managed to seek help from a woman trader before his father called his wife to pick him up.
A police report was later lodged.
Police urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Seri Alam district police control centre at 07-3871422 or its hotline at 07-3861422.

Title: Malaysia may one day vote online, EC says trust and security top priorities
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — The Election Commission (EC) has not ruled out the possibility of introducing online or electronic voting in Malaysia in the future.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the proposal would however, require thorough study, particularly in terms of public trust and confidence in such a system.
He explained that several critical aspects must be considered, including cybersecurity, the integrity of the electoral process, ballot secrecy, infrastructure readiness and potential legislative amendments.
“The EC is examining the possibility of implementing e voting before it is introduced in Malaysia. Among the matters being reviewed are the experiences of other countries, current technological developments, system security and integrity, as well as the level of public readiness,” he told BH.
General elections are held when Parliament or a state assembly is dissolved, while by elections take place to fill unexpected vacancies.
On polling day, registered voters cast their ballots at designated centres between 8am and 6pm in Peninsular Malaysia, and from 7.30am to 5.30pm in Sabah and Sarawak.

Title: No water, no stay: KK hotels hit by cancellations amid supply cuts since Aug 8
Article:
KOTA KINABLAU, Aug 14 — A water supply disruption in the State Capital has affected 14 hotels since Wednesday (Aug 12), according to the Malaysian Association of Hotels (MAH) Sabah and Labuan Chapter.
Its chairman, Suresh Ramasamy, urged the Sabah Water Department to urgently stabilise and restore supply, noting that initial disruptions involving several premises had begun as early as Aug 8.
He said affected hotels were forced to rely on reserve tanks and costly private water tankers, which are facing severe availability constraints due to simultaneous demand from businesses and residential areas.
The ongoing supply issue has already triggered room cancellations and shortened stays, threatening broader financial repercussions for local tour operators, transport providers, and businesses.
Warning that prolonged multi-day uncertainty could weaken tourism confidence ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026 and Visit Sabah Year 2027, MAH called for priority tanker assistance and clearer restoration timelines for affected premises. — Daily Express

Title: ‘Party within the party’: Nurul Izzah says PKR unity threatened by internal clashes
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — PKR’s deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar has cautioned that the party cannot remain strong if it is distracted by internal disputes.
Speaking at the joint Wanita Keadilan and Angkatan Muda Keadilan congress in Ayer Keroh today, she said the party risked weakening itself if factionalism continued to dominate,
The Star
reported.
“We cannot be strong as an organisation if there is a party within the party, two captains steering one ship, or the existence of an invisible hand, a hidden power structure behind the visible power structure,” she was quoted as saying in her opening address.
She said the party could not be strong if its energy continued to be consumed by internal disputes, noting that every hour spent quarrelling among members was time lost in winning public support.
Nurul Izzah also highlighted that PKR’s priorities should remain focused on democratising the economy, competing to do good and securing electoral victories. She acknowledged that not every task would be easy.
Her remarks come in the wake of several high profile departures from the party, including former leaders Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad.
The PKR national congress, which began yesterday, is scheduled to conclude on Sunday.

Title: Paid to remove bad luck, lost a fortune instead: Police say ritual scam cost Sabah victims RM600,000
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — Police have detained 12 people, including seven Chinese women, over an alleged “Chinese-medium” scam linked to losses of about RM600,000.
State DCP Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin said the suspects, comprising 10 women and two men, were believed to be linked to a syndicate that had been operating since early this year.
He said the syndicate allegedly offered fortune-telling, traditional treatment and rituals to remove bad luck.
The arrests were made during raids in Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Keningau and Kota Belud last Saturday and Sunday by the Sabah Police Commercial Crime Investigation Department, with assistance from district commercial crime investigation teams.
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah's Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn't mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
Mohd Azhar said four suspects were detained during raids in Kota Kinabalu and Keningau on Saturday, while eight more, including seven Chinese women, were detained in Kota Belud the following day.
He said the syndicate allegedly approached victims by offering traditional medicine, treatment for illnesses or rituals to remove bad luck.
The suspects would then introduce another woman who claimed she could tell fortunes, provide treatment or perform rituals.
“Victims were persuaded to hand over cash or jewellery, supposedly for prayers, incantations or rituals.
“The money or jewellery would then be taken away or replaced with other items placed inside a plastic bag or another bag,” he said.
Mohd Azhar said victims were usually told not to open the bag for a certain period, giving the suspects time to escape.
The syndicate is believed to be linked to at least five or six reported cases in Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Sandakan since early this year, with total losses estimated at about RM600,000.
The cases are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Daily Express

Title: Serian has Malaysia’s worst air quality with API at 183, Kuching and Samarahan tie at 171 while Cheras chokes in the peninsula
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — As of 10am today, 10 locations across Malaysia recorded unhealthy air quality levels, with most of them concentrated in Sarawak.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Serian registered the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183, followed closely by Kuching (171), Samarahan (171), Sri Aman (163), Sarikei (158), Mukah (152) and Bintulu (147).
In Peninsular Malaysia, three areas posted unhealthy readings: Cheras (153), Johan Setia (150), and Shah Alam (103).
Meanwhile, 56 locations recorded moderate API levels (51-100), while only two areas registered good air quality (below 50).
The API scale is as follows: 0-50 (Good), 51-100 (Moderate), 101-200 (Unhealthy), 201-300 (Very Unhealthy), and above 300 (Hazardous).
API readings are released hourly, based on data from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: ‘Somebody has to pay’: Serian chief says Sarawakians are fed up with yearly haze from Kalimantan Barat
Article:
SERIAN, Aug 14 — Serian District Council chairman Dato Peter Minos has voiced his frustration over the worsening haze, saying the town’s iconic mountain view had been “lost in the haze”.
He said residents were asking where the mountain range, normally visible from the Serian District Council building, had gone when he was in Serian at 10am on Thursday.
According to Minos, Serian was experiencing its worst haze situation in recent years, which he attributed to smoke from Kalimantan Barat, Indonesia, being blown into the area by prevailing winds.
He said many were anxious after the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Serian reached 202 on Wednesday, a level classified as very unhealthy.
“The haze is one big headache for us in Sarawak, being a bad health hazard. The hardest hit are our young children and the elderly,” he said.
He also pointed out that all schools in Serian had been ordered to close due to the deteriorating air quality, questioning when they would be able to reopen.
Minos questioned why the authorities in Kalimantan Barat appeared unable to prevent open burning, particularly by large oil palm estates during planting activities.
“If we Malaysians can do it, why can’t they? We just do not burn. And if we burn, NREB will hit us hard,” he said, referring to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB).
He said the recurring haze had affected Sarawak year after year, causing losses beyond health impacts, including school closures and reduced tourism revenue.
Expressing his frustration, Minos said Sarawakians were “unhappy and fed up” with the recurring haze.
“It gets on our nerves. Haze is human-created, not natural, and so somebody has to pay for it,” he said.

Title: Sri Muda petrol station brawl sees man slashed with machete, police confirm investigation underway
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — A man was left with serious injuries to his left hand following an alleged machete attack during a fight involving several individuals in Sri Muda yesterday.
According to
The Star
, the incident reportedly occurred around 11am near a petrol station along Jalan Bukit Kemuning. The 38 year old victim is currently receiving treatment at Klang Hospital.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said officers received a report from the injured man and have since opened investigations.
He said police are investigating the case under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting while armed, Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a weapon, and Section 8 of the Arms Act 1960 for possession of an object resembling a firearm.
ACP Sarudin urged members of the public with information to assist police by contacting investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Shamsiah Noor Zakaria at 012 830 8706.

Title: Valve fault delays water supply recovery for 15,000 Sibu consumers
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 14 — Repair works on the 1,000mm-diameter main pipeline near Lorong Kiew Nang 1 in Sibu were completed early Friday morning, but water supply could not be restored immediately to all affected consumers due to a malfunctioning delivery valve.
In a statement, Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd said during the restoration process, a 600mm-diameter delivery valve at the Salim Water Treatment Plant experienced an unexpected malfunction, which further affected the recovery of water supply to several areas.
“Repair works on the affected valve are currently ongoing and are expected to be completed between 1pm and 3pm on Friday. Consumers are advised that water supply will not return to normal immediately upon completion of the valve repair works,” the utility company said.
Sarawak Water said approximately 15,000 consumers in several areas in Sibu are expected to continue experiencing temporary water supply interruption or low water pressure.
The areas are Jalan Tun Ahmad Zaidi Adruce (Jalan Salim intersection) – Lorong 60 to Lorong 66, including the Petronas Station; Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, including Lorong Tunku Abdul Rahman 42, Rumah Sebastian, Jalan Rafflesia, Jalan Jade Villa, Taman Primeview, Taman Azalea, Taman Sanhill, Sibu Airport, and Eco Garden; Sibu Jaya; Jalan Durin Link up to Durin Bridge; Jalan Satria, Jalan Bumi Indah, Jalan Ruai, Jalan Bougenvilla, Jalan Kaland, Jalan Pine, Taman Kemuyang, Rascom Camp, and Rumah Nari up to the Sibu–Bintulu junction; as well as surrounding areas.
Sarawak Water said water supply would be restored progressively, with some areas receiving supply earlier than others depending on their location within the distribution system.
In the meantime, the company has deployed water tankers to the affected areas to provide temporary water supply assistance while repair and restoration efforts are ongoing.
During the recovery period, some consumers may experience temporary low water pressure or discoloured water as the distribution system stabilises, it explained.
Consumers experiencing discoloured water are advised to allow their taps to run until the water becomes clear before use.
Sarawak Water apologised for the inconvenience caused and appreciates the patience and understanding of all affected consumers as its teams work to restore the water supply as soon as possible.
Further updates on the repair works and water supply restoration progress will be provided through Sarawak Water’s official communication channels. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police investigate Pasir Mas classroom clash as teacher allegedly hits pupil and mother with cane
Article:
PASIR MAS, Aug 14 — Police have detained a 54 year old teacher accused of assaulting a pupil and the boy’s mother with a cane in two separate incidents this week.
According to
Harian Metro
, the arrest followed a report lodged by the mother, who alleged her son — a pupil at a primary school in Pasir Mas — was struck by the teacher. Investigators later found the boy had earlier been hit on the head with a cane at school on August 11.
The mother raised the matter with the school, prompting the headmaster to arrange a meeting the next day. During the discussion, held in the headmaster’s office, the teacher allegedly shouted and struck the woman on her right thigh with the cane. The incident was witnessed by the headmaster, who was said to be shocked by the teacher’s actions. The woman fled in fear.
Police said the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a weapon, an offence that carries up to 10 years’ jail, or fine, or whipping, or any two of those punishments upon conviction.
The teacher has been remanded for three days until Saturday.

Title: Toyota van driver dead, five passengers injured after collision with lorry on North-South highway near Kluang
Article:
KLUANG, Aug 14 — A woman was killed while five others were injured in an accident involving a van and a lorry at KM55.1 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) northbound early this morning.
Renggam Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) operations commander Shoromi Salih said five personnel and a Sitrak fire and rescue vehicle were dispatched to the scene, located 51 kilometres away, upon receiving a report. They arrived at 12.54 am.
“The driver of the Toyota van, a woman, was confirmed dead at the scene after becoming trapped in the driver’s section,” he said in a statement.
The five passengers in the van, including three children and a disabled man, were injured and removed from the vehicle by members of the public before the firefighters arrived.
He said the male driver of the Isuzu lorry was reported to be safe and uninjured. — Bernama

Title: ‘I will continue saving’: Tabung Haji depositors stand by institution despite RCI spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Although Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has come under the spotlight again following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on issues concerning its management and operations, depositors’ confidence in the institution as a ‘trustee’ in helping them realise their dream of performing haj remains unwavering.
For the majority of Muslims in Malaysia, TH is not merely an ordinary financial, savings and investment institution. Instead, it bears the significant responsibility of helping depositors fulfil a deeply meaningful religious and spiritual obligation.
This was acknowledged by tailor Atiqah Shah Hadi, 40, who continues to place her full trust in the institution to manage her savings in her TH account, which she has maintained for decades.
“As far as I can remember, my father opened a TH account for me when I was still young, and I once checked with one of TH’s branches some time ago. I was told that my expected turn to perform haj would be in 2033.
“Of course, I will continue saving with TH to ensure that when the time comes, and I am blessed with the opportunity to become a TH haj pilgrim, I will have sufficient savings,” she told Bernama.
Meanwhile, civil servant Muhammad Haikal Abdul Halim, 35, said he was aware of the issues surrounding the institution responsible for managing haj affairs, but as a depositor, he had never considered withdrawing his existing savings.
“In fact, I plan to set up a monthly salary deduction in the near future for deposits into my TH account because, based on the current haj waiting list, I am expected to have the opportunity to perform haj in 2032. Therefore, preparations must be made from now,” he said.
Muhammad Haikal also said he intended to open TH savings accounts for his three children, aged seven, four and three.
Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Centre for Economic Development and Policy director Dr Saizal Pinjaman said that two key aspects that TH needed to emphasise to maintain public confidence were safeguarding depositors’ savings and strengthening its long-term financial and business capabilities.
“To safeguard these priorities, TH must determine its profits based on accounts that have been transparently audited, while taking into account all losses, impairment of investments and assets. All these depend on economic conditions and other fundamentals.
“Additionally, TH needs to maintain sufficient reserves to withstand any changes in the market. Ultimately, profits should only be distributed when there is a balance that can genuinely be afforded for payment to depositors,” he said.
Saizal said TH should also consistently provide details on the actual cost of haj assistance that it had incurred or was currently bearing.
For analyst Dr Noor Nirwandy Mat Noordin, the post-crisis period experienced by TH had seen the institution bounce back stronger, to the extent that it had been recognised as one of the best haj management organisations in the world in recent years.
The senior lecturer at the Centre for Media and Information Warfare Studies, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Shah Alam, expressed confidence that TH would continue to discharge the trust and mandate of Muslims in the country effectively, excellently and in a manner they could be proud of. — Bernama

Title: It’s up to you, parents: Sarawak minister says won’t shut kindergartens, childcare centres even if API is over 200
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 14 — Kindergartens (Tadika) and childcare centres (Taska) in Sarawak may continue operating during the current haze to accommodate children whose parents need to work, said Dato Sri Fatimah Abdullah.
The State Women, Early Childhood and Community Wellbeing Development Minister said this was despite the existing measure requiring Tadika and Taska to close when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200 and above.
“Attendance at Tadika and Taska should remain at the discretion or choice of parents.
“These centres are the essential support systems for working parents,” she said in a statement.
Fatimah, who is also a member of the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC), said the centres could provide a safer and more controlled environment for children, provided they had air-conditioning, appropriate air filtration or purification systems and proper standard operating procedures (SOPs).
She said children who were unwell should remain at home, while those attending the centres would be screened upon arrival to ensure they were fit before being admitted.
“If a child develops symptoms while at the centre, parents will be contacted to bring the child back,” she said.
Fatimah said all outdoor activities at Tadika and Taska should also be suspended during the haze.
“For journeys between home and the centres, parents should ensure that their children wear masks and minimise their exposure to the outdoors.
“For children with asthma, respiratory conditions and other vulnerabilities, they should ensure the prescribed inhalers are brought along with their children while also informing the centre of their child’s condition and care requirements,” she advised.
Parents should also ensure their children drink sufficient water and remain adequately hydrated throughout the day, she added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Haze? Penang schools ready to call off outdoor activities once API crosses 100, shut if over 200
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Schools in areas recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading will be required to suspend all outdoor activities involving students as a precautionary measure amid the haze affecting Penang.
Penang Education Department (JPNPP) director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said data from the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed that the Minden monitoring station recorded an API reading in the “unhealthy” category yesterday afternoon.
“We are monitoring API levels periodically. In accordance with Ministry of Education guidelines, schools in areas with ‘unhealthy’ API readings will continue to operate as usual, but all outdoor activities involving students will be suspended as a precautionary measure,” he said when contacted by Bernama last night.
He said seven schools in the Minden area, comprising four primary and three secondary schools, are affected.
“Should the API level remain in the ‘unhealthy’ range [this] morning, these schools will suspend all outdoor activities,” he said.
The DOE APIMS data showed that the Minden station recorded an API reading of 107 at noon and 103 an hour later before falling to 97 at 3 pm. The latest reading at 8 pm was 96, placing it in the “moderate” category.
Meanwhile, the Balik Pulau, Seberang Perai and Seberang Jaya monitoring stations recorded API readings between 84 and 95 at 8 pm, also within the “moderate” range.
Mohamad Dziauddin said he would meet all headmasters and principals at 11am today to provide the latest updates and outline the necessary measures should the haze situation worsen or API readings reach unhealthy levels.
He advised students to wear face masks and stay adequately hydrated, while schools should immediately refer any students who become unwell to their parents or guardians.
Under the guidelines for school management during haze episodes, schools must suspend all outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100.
If the API exceeds 200, all schools in the affected area or district must close immediately, while teachers and support staff are not required to report for duty if the API exceeds 500.
The guidelines also stipulate that schools may reopen when the API falls below 200 and shows a downward trend. — Bernama

Title: Heart attack suspected after woman crashes MPV into two parked motorcycles in George Town
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — A woman died after she was believed to have suffered a heart attack while driving a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) this afternoon, before crashing into two motorcycles parked by the roadside along Jalan Macalister here.
Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the 36-year-old woman died while receiving treatment at Penang Hospital.
“The accident only involved the MPV driver, while the two motorcycles seen in the viral video were unoccupied and parked by the roadside outside a restaurant.
“A post-mortem will be conducted to determine the exact cause of death,” he said in a statement tonight.
Earlier, a 1.52-minute video went viral on social media showing a car crashing into two motorcycles outside a restaurant, in an incident believed to have occurred at about 2pm yesterday. — Bernama

Title: PKR must look in the mirror, not blame voters, says Youth chief
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — PKR must have the courage to reflect on its performance following recent state elections instead of blaming voters for its defeats, Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim said.
He said while election victories boosted confidence, defeats should instead provide an opportunity for the party to reflect and address its weaknesses, while identifying the reasons why some people remain unconvinced by the party.
“The results of the (several) recent state elections must be viewed with courage. Do not blame the people at all. Do not be angry with voters for not choosing us.
“The people do not owe any party their votes; we are the ones who owe the people an explanation,” he said in his policy speech at the AMK National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here yesterday.
Muhammad Kamil said PKR needed to provide better answers to narratives by certain quarters seeking to create concern among voters by playing on issues of the Malays and Islam being under threat under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership.
He said failure to address public concerns would allow others to fill the void with narratives based on fear and suspicion, requiring PKR to offer a “politics of confidence” that ensures Malay interests and Islam’s position remain protected within a framework of a fair and diverse Malaysia.
“We have a duty to provide better answers to these concerns because if we leave that space empty, others will fill it with fear.
“If we do not provide confidence, others will sell it through suspicion. Therefore, we must offer something greater, namely a politics of confidence,” he added. — Bernama

Title: BUDI95 quota too low? PKR Youth wants 300 litres restored, 350 litres for high-mileage users
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — The PKR Youth wing (AMK) wants the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) fuel quota restored to 300 litres and raised to 350 litres for those with high mobility needs, based on clear usage data.
AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim said the call took into account lower global oil prices and the country’s fiscal space, which he said provided room for the government to raise the subsidy quota.
“We are not asking for unlimited subsidies. We are asking for a policy that understands the realities of people’s lives because subsidy reform must go hand in hand with reforms that benefit the people.
“If the people are asked to make sacrifices, they have the right to see dividends from those sacrifices,” he said in his policy speech at the AMK National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here last night.
He also called for the Bumiputera empowerment policy to be strengthened so that the next generation would not merely receive protection, but have the capacity to become owners in strategic areas, including housing, property, shares, companies, intellectual property and technology.
“Malay youths must have skills in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors, green technology, biotechnology, aerospace, engineering and cybersecurity.
“We do not want Malay youths to merely be users of technology created by others. We want them to be creators,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anthony Loke’s transport push: LRT3 opens, ridership surges past one million, but congestion fight unfinished
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Nearly four years into his second stint as transport minister, Anthony Loke can point to gains in public transport and rail use, but says Malaysia’s growing vehicle population, ageing infrastructure and gaps in connectivity continue to complicate efforts to overhaul the country’s transport system.
One of the areas where Loke has sought to make the biggest changes is Prasarana Malaysia Berhad, which operates the Klang Valley’s Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and monorail services.
Loke said Prasarana was in poor shape when he returned to the ministry in late 2022, with frequent disruptions and maintenance problems affecting public confidence.
“Prasarana at the end of 2022 was in a really bad shape. And in terms of maintenance, in terms of a lot of disruption. Public confidence towards Prasarana was extremely low,” he told
Malay Mail
in an interview.
“Even simple things are not running. Escalators in the station are not running, the light bulbs are out, toilets are not functioning, trains disrupted and so forth,” he said.
Loke said his first act as minister was to conduct a spot check at an MRT station to signal his focus on Prasarana.
“That is to send a message, to set the tone and send a message. And I wanted to focus on Prasarana,” he said.
He subsequently made Prasarana a permanent feature of post-Cabinet meetings and required the company to report on key performance indicators, particularly maintenance and service disruptions.
“I made it a point that they have to report everything on the key parameters and the dashboard, and drove them to focus on maintenance,” he said.
The number of disruptions fell in 2024 and 2025, although the situation deteriorated again in early 2026, particularly on the ageing Kelana Jaya Line, while additional trains planned for the line have yet to arrive.
“By and large, compared to 2022, our scenario is in a better shape today in terms of the overall operations, in terms of the overall planning and management,” he said.
Rail use grows as vehicle numbers climb
The LRT3 Shah Alam Line at Johan Setia Station, Klang, June 28, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Loke said the recovery in urban rail use to pre-Covid levels showed that public transport demand remained strong, with certain lines including the Kelana Jaya Line now facing overcrowding and ridership continuing to rise following the opening of the LRT3 Shah Alam Line.
“We have consistently surpassed one million in daily ridership.
“But the growth in rail use is happening alongside a continuing increase in vehicles on Malaysian roads.
“But can you imagine without that the rail system, the traffic will be even worse off, right?” he said.
Malaysia recorded more than 700,000 vehicle sales last year, Loke said, reflecting a structural problem that has made it difficult to reduce congestion despite continued investment in public transport.
“This is a structural issue which not many people would understand, you know, people complain why traffic jam is still ongoing, without realising that the car population is increasing,” he said.
Loke said Malaysia’s automotive policy had encouraged vehicle ownership but lacked a corresponding policy to take older cars off the road.
“The car population will increase every day,” he said.
However, he said introducing an end-of-life vehicle policy would be difficult because many Malaysians still depend on older cars, particularly in semi-urban areas.
“And in our country, it’s not that practical yet, because not everyone can afford to get a newer car,” he said.
“And there is a real need for vehicles, especially in the semi-urban areas.
“Malaysia’s dispersed population also means public transport cannot reach every corner of the country.
“The fact is that, public transport cannot reach every corner of the country,” Loke said.
Bridging the first and last mile
The ministry has sought to address that gap through Demand Responsive Transit (DRT) services operated by Prasarana in the Klang Valley, alongside feeder buses linking residential areas with rail stations.
Loke said there were about 380 points for DRT services, but landed housing areas, particularly on the outskirts of the Klang Valley, remained difficult to serve.
“On the outskirts of Klang Valley, we have a lot of landed properties, and landed housing estates, which make it difficult for the last mile and first mile to reach every corner in every household,” he said.
“We know, for example, the buses, they will not be able to serve every single lane or every single house in the housing estates.”
The ministry has also sought to encourage carpooling and ride-sharing, but Loke said the varied needs of commuters meant there was no single solution.
“We try multiple approaches, but there will not be a one-size-fits-all kind of solution,” he said.
Loke said the ministry has also sought to encourage carpooling and ride-sharing, but the varied needs of commuters meant there was no single solution. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Moving more cargo onto rail
Beyond moving passengers, Loke wants to make greater use of Malaysia’s railway network to transport cargo, with the ministry acquiring more locomotives, refurbishing older ones and adding wagons to increase freight capacity.
The government is also pushing for a rolling stock leasing programme between Malaysia and China to secure more trains and enable additional passenger services.
Loke said the railway network was a strategic national asset that had not been fully utilised.
“Railway is actually a very strategic asset of the country, which in the past we have not really fully utilised,” he said.
With the double-track railway network, the upcoming East Coast Rail Link and other upgrading projects, the government wants to create a rail artery across the peninsula for both passengers and cargo.
“We want to have this artery of transport network throughout peninsula so that we can connect the entire peninsula by railway, not only just for passengers but also for cargo,” he said.
The network would also connect major ports including Port Klang, Penang Port and Port of Tanjung Pelepas.
One project the ministry is pushing for is the Southern Bypass Line, which would connect Seremban directly to Port Klang and allow cargo trains from the south to bypass Kuala Lumpur.
Loke said freight trains from the south currently had to pass through Kuala Lumpur before heading to Port Klang, creating a bottleneck as cargo services shared the network with passenger trains.
If approved by the Ministry of Economy and Ministry of Finance, he said, the bypass would allow cargo from the south to travel directly to Port Klang.
Road safety remains a priority
Road safety, particularly involving heavy vehicles, has also taken up a significant part of the ministry’s work, with two major tragedies last year intensifying scrutiny of public service and heavy vehicles.
“Two tragedies happened within a month, which, you know, caused a lot of public concern and debate,” he said.
The ministry subsequently rolled out measures including stricter enforcement and regulation, new safety technologies and wider use of telematics systems.
Loke acknowledged that the measures came at a cost to operators and faced industry pushback, but said safety could not be compromised.
“But, safety is something which we have to deal with seriously,” he said.
Airfares remain largely market-driven
On airfares, Loke said the government had limited room to intervene as ticket prices were largely determined by market forces. — Picture by Yusof Isa
On airfares, Loke said the government had limited room to intervene as ticket prices were largely determined by market forces.
Malaysia does not have a policy of capping airline ticket prices except during selected major festive periods for flights between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak, with the fare cap applying for about 12 to 14 days a year during major festivals including Chinese New Year, Hari Raya, Gawai and Christmas.
“We can’t afford to cap the fares every day,” he said.
Loke attributed higher airfares partly to increased jet fuel prices, which he said had risen by 30 to 40 per cent, as well as airlines cutting capacity because of higher operating costs.
“To be fair to the airlines, most airlines are trying to keep flying, even though they have some reduction in capacity, but overall it’s not that many,” he said.
The ministry has been engaging airlines to maintain basic connectivity while encouraging them to restore capacity, with most airlines agreeing to review their normal flight schedules by September and October.
“We have tried to encourage the airlines to slowly bring back their capacity,” Loke said.
For Loke, however, the work across Malaysia’s transport sector has no clear endpoint.
“Public transport is a never-ending effort,” he said.
“It’s not that we have done this and it’s finished.”

Title: Uncharted territories: Anthony Loke on alliances, unity constraints and search for lasting model
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia is still searching for a permanent model of governance eight years after the collapse of the country’s decades-old political order, with parties continuing to adjust to shifting alliances and electoral calculations, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said the political landscape had gone through multiple permutations and collaborations since 2018, with political actors continuing to work out arrangements they believe could strengthen their positions.
“As I say, we are into uncharted territories right now,” he told
Malay Mail
in an interview.
“After the collapse of the decades-old model in 2018, I think we are still trying to find a permanent model, a permanent model of governance in Malaysia,” he said.
Loke said political parties and politicians would continue making calculations based on their chances of winning elections and remaining in power.
“Political parties and politicians will continue to calculate their function. They want to maximise their political function,” he said.
“And I think from 2018 until now, we have experienced different permutations, different calibrations.
“But as far as I’m concerned, I think it’s not going to end soon. So this will keep evolving,” he said.
Balancing party and government
The shifting political landscape has also left Loke navigating the competing demands of his roles as DAP secretary-general and Cabinet minister in the Unity Government, where the party works alongside former political rivals including Barisan Nasional.
Asked whether DAP had changed after becoming part of the government, Loke said the party had not abandoned its positions, but had to operate within the constraints of a unity government.
“No (the party has not changed). Of course, we need to coordinate, we need to work within the constraint of a unity government,” he said.
Loke said DAP leaders would continue articulating the party’s positions, while ministers had to observe collective responsibility within the Cabinet.
“As a secretary-general, of course I have to carry the position of the party, but at the same time I’m leading the Cabinet, so I have to carry that expression in the government.
“So I have to play that role in a very challenging way,” he said.
He said this meant he could not publicly criticise Cabinet colleagues, coalition parties or government policy while serving as part of the administration.
The shifting political landscape has also left Loke navigating the competing demands of his roles as DAP secretary-general and Cabinet minister in the Unity Government, where the party works alongside former political rivals including Barisan Nasional.
Transport Minister. — Picture by Yusof Isa
“Being part of the government, say for example, I cannot criticise another Cabinet member or the parties that are within the coalition government, that will be out of line in terms of collective responsibility,” he said.
“Nor can I criticise the government’s policy, because I’m part of the government,” he said.
At the same time, Loke said DAP could still take positions critical of government policies or actions, creating a delicate balance for the party as it remains part of the ruling coalition.
“But at the same time, sometimes the party takes a different position, and takes a position which is critical to the government’s policy or government’s action.
“So this is a situation where we have to face,” Loke said.
Loke said major decisions would continue to be brought before DAP’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) so the party could reach a common position.
“As far as I know, I mean any major decision will be brought back to the Central Executive Committee (CEC) for a common opinion or common position and a common decision that will be made by the CEC,” he said.
Political alliances will keep changing
Loke acknowledged that some political developments could be disappointing, but said parties would continue making decisions based on their electoral interests as Malaysia adjusts to its post-2018 political reality.
The shifting relationship between PH and BN was evident in the state elections, with the two federal coalition partners contesting separately in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
In Johor, BN contested all 56 seats on its own, with state leaders citing the state’s political circumstances and grassroots views. PH subsequently announced it would also contest all 56 seats.
In Negeri Sembilan, BN initially remained open to working with PH but later decided to contest independently after PH announced it would contest all 36 seats
“This is something which is disappointing, but it happens.
“We have to, we just have to soldier on. We have to keep the faith alive,” Loke said.
He said political actors would continue searching for a governing arrangement that would put them in control, but ultimately the direction of Malaysian politics would depend on voters.
“I think political parties, different political actors will continue to search for a model which everyone of course would hope that they are in charge, they want to be in control,” he said.
“I think the public has to realise what is at stake and we have to soldier on, but at the end of the day, it’s the choice of the voters.”

Title: No tyre marks, no crushed bones: Defence challenges eyewitness accounts in murder trial of senior cop accused of running down teen with Ativa
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — The High Court here today heard that 17-year-old Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie was not run over by the vehicle driven by senior police officer DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, as claimed by eyewitnesses.
In his submission at the close of the prosecution’s case before Judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet, lead defence counsel M. Athimulan argued that the “run over” theory was inconsistent with objective forensic and medical evidence.
He pointed out that the forensic pathologist had confirmed that the victim’s injuries were not consistent with being run over, as there were no crushed bones, destroyed organs, or tyre marks on the deceased’s body or clothing.
“My Lord, we respectfully submit that this medical evidence is a scientific and objective truth; it is not prone to the fallibility of human perception. It directly refutes the eyewitnesses’ core claim,” he submitted.
He contended that the eyewitness accounts were inherently unreliable because they were contradicted by expert medical evidence.
Athimulan said the absence of tyre marks on the deceased’s body and shirt supported the defence’s submission that the incident was a tragedy in which the teenager was “thrown” from the motorcycle upon contact, rather than intentionally “run over”, with the injuries suffered being consistent with a fall on the road.
He said the medical evidence completely ruled out all probabilities of the ocular evidence (direct oral testimony of an eyewitness) being true and, therefore, the defence counsel team respectfully submitted that the ocular evidence should be rejected.
“The eyewitness’s testimonies were flawed with perception of a traumatic event and influenced by social media impact,” he said.
Furthermore, Athimulan addressed the critical implications from the failure to tender “black box” (Event Data Records – EDR) data from the Perodua Ativa, particularly as the data was central to reconstructing the incident and determining mens rea (intent) under Section 300 of the Penal Code.
“It is respectfully submitted that, without black box data, the prosecution cannot prove whether the accused attempted to brake, or the accused swerved, or tried to avoid the collision, and whether the speed was consistent with loss of control rather than deliberate aim.
“My Lord, we are submitting that these are not minor gaps, but they are central to the prosecution’s theory of malicious intent. The charge against the accused is a most serious crime under the Penal Code, alleging murder by means of intentional vehicular conduct,” Athimulan said.
Deputy public prosecutors Afzainizam Abdul Aziz, Nasrul Hadi Abdul Ghani and Monisha Pandey appeared for the prosecution.
The accused was represented by a legal team comprising Athimulan, Datuk Mior Faridalathrash Wahid and Aiman Hakim Kamaruzzaman.
The trial will resume at 10 am tomorrow.
Mohd Nazri was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif Affendi near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Jati on Dec 15, 2023, between 11.55 am and 12.32 pm.
The offence is punishable with either a death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, plus a minimum of 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: ‘I’m still in the Unity Govt’: Lahad Datu MP Yusof Apdal says viral resignation claim ‘untrue and malicious’
Article:
LAHAD DATU, Aug 13 — Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal today denied claims that he had resigned and withdrawn from the federal government.
In a statement to Bernama today, he said the claim circulating on social media was untrue and malicious.
“I remain a member of the Unity Government administration and continue to carry out the trust and responsibilities entrusted to me,” he said.
He said the dissemination of such false information not only misled the public, but was also intended to tarnish his reputation.
Mohammad Yusof, who is also the Lahad Datu Member of Parliament from Parti Warisan, urged the public not to spread unverified news and to always refer to official sources for accurate and authentic information.
Today, a social media post circulated claiming that Mohammad Yusof had decided to resign as Deputy Minister, effective today. — Bernama

Title: If it feels like this haze has been here forever, you’re right — and 10 areas in Klang Valley and Sarawak are still recording unhealthy air pollution levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — A total of 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian with an API reading of 178, Samarahan (177), Kuching (174), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (157), Mukah (152) and Sibu (151).
In the Peninsula, three areas also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Johan Setia (154) and Shah Alam (108) in Selangor, as well as Cheras (127) in Kuala Lumpur.
Meanwhile, 56 areas recorded API readings at the moderate level, while two areas recorded good readings.
API readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: RM19,000 in alleged bribes lands Pahang agency official in MACC custody
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained a female official from a government agency in Pahang over allegations of soliciting and receiving around RM19,000 in bribes to help secure tenders and contracts at another agency in the state.
Sources said the woman, in her 30s, was detained at about 6.45pm yesterday while giving a statement at the Temerloh MACC office.
“Preliminary findings suggest the suspect carried out the acts between 2016 and 2021, receiving bribes from various companies and individuals directly into her personal bank account,” the source disclosed.
The woman has been remanded for five days until Aug 19 after Magistrate Anis Adlina Abu Johan granted an application by the MACC at the Kuantan Magistrate’s Court today.
Meanwhile, Pahang MACC director Mohamad Shukor Mahmud, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB strikes a deal to drop its civil suit against former CFO, trial continues for Najib and five others
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and its former chief financial officer (CFO) Radhi Mohamad have struck a deal today to withdraw the US$5.64 billion civil suit against him, with both parties agreeing to record a consent order in court.
1MDB counsel Lee Shih confirmed that Radhi, 55, and the plaintiffs, 1MDB and its four subsidiaries, had reached an agreement on the terms of the consent order and would file it in court today.
“My Lord, I can confirm that the plaintiffs and the sixth defendant would like to record a consent judgment or consent order today.
“Under the consent order, the suit against Radhi would be discontinued, with no liberty to file afresh,” he submitted.
The matter was subsequently confirmed by Radhi’s lawyer Datuk M. Reza Hassan.
After hearing submissions, High Court Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus ruled that the sixth defendant should be struck out as a co-defendant in the proceedings.
“Much obliged to all the parties for taking the time to settle this matter,” he said.
The trial for the US$5.64 billion suit entered its eighth day today, with three witnesses for the plaintiffs having taken the stand so far.
The afternoon session of the proceedings was resumed with former 1MDB chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi reading his witness statement.
1MDB and its subsidiaries – 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited – filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh, Radhi, former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial resumes on Monday. — Bernama

Title: Space, gas and more: Russia and Malaysia eye new areas to work together
Article:
VLADIVOSTOK, Aug 13 — Russia sees prospects for a partnership with Malaysia in the space industry, Russian Minister of Science and Higher Education Valery Falkov said on Thursday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
The fifth meeting of the Joint Russian-Malaysian Commission on Economic, Scientific, Technical and Cultural Cooperation opened in Vladivostok on Thursday.
“There are prospects for Russia-Malaysia partnership in the space sector. A Russian company has already built and launched a satellite for Malaysia into orbit,” Falkov, the commission’s co-chairman, told reporters.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said that Russia and Malaysia also have significant opportunities for cooperation in the energy sector, including liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas. — Bernama-Sputnik/Ria Novosti
